name: Singapore University of Social Sciences
description: The Singapore University of Social Sciences is a public university in Clementi, Singapore, established in 2005 as SIM University and renamed and brought under the Ministry of Education as an Autonomous University in 2017. It focuses on the social sciences, business, law and lifelong learning, with both full-time and part-time degree programmes.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded Autonomous Universities, and the local option for social-science, business and part-time degrees that Singaporean students compare against overseas fees.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Laws (LLB)
programmes.summary: Part-time evening degree for Citizens and PRs only; not open to international students. Programme total spread over about 4.5 years at the Tuition Grant rate. Fees are reviewed each year.
programmes.notes: NOT OPEN TO INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: SUSS's law-programmes eligibility page states 'The Law programme is open to Singaporeans and Permanent Residents only. This programme is unable to enrol international students or non-citizens.' The 'international' tier is kept only because the schema requires it: it is the 'Estimated Total Programme Fee (Without Government Tuition Grant, including GST)' that SUSS publishes for any student without the Tuition Grant (e.g. a Citizen or PR who is ineligible for or has used up the MOE Tuition Grant), not an international-student fee. Part-time, evening programme: SUSS's School of Law brochure (Jan 2026) says both law degrees 'comprise classes conducted in the evenings', are modular and allow students 'to continue working'; SUSS offers no full-time law programme (law is not in its full-time undergraduate list; checked 2026-10-01). Entry criteria (SUSS eligibility page and Jan 2026 brochure): Singapore Citizen or PR; GCE A Level (three H2 passes), local polytechnic diploma, IB Diploma or NUS High School Diploma; the LNAT; English and Mother Tongue Language requirements; admission interview. All applicants other than fresh school leavers must submit a CV of their work experience, and SUSS says recruitment gives preference to applicants with 'a fair amount of work experience' (e.g. social work, law enforcement, prison service) or current community-work involvement; MinLaw's 2016 press release set the school up for 'mature students with life and work experience seeking a mid-career switch to law' (at least 80% of the intake). SUSS states no minimum age for the LLB, and fresh A Level/diploma holders may apply, but it is not a typical school-leaver programme. Fees: SUSS School of Law 'Bachelor of Laws' Year 2026 programme fees (PDF updated 13 Mar 2026, linked as 'Year 2026 Bachelor of Laws' from the law tuition-fees page). Fees are charged per course (with MOE Tuition Grant, excluding GST: SC S$1,302 / PR S$2,072 per 5-cu course). SUSS's 'Estimated Total Programme Fee': SC S$46,840 and PR S$74,600 (with Tuition Grant, excl. GST, separately subsidised by the government); without Tuition Grant S$199,066 incl. 9% GST. Annual figure = published total programme fee / 4.5 years, SUSS's stated typical completion time (180 cu; LLB page: 'about 4.5 years'; all School of Law students must finish within a maximum of 6 years), so a slower student pays the same total over more years. July intake (from 2026 the law academic year starts in July). Compulsory fees = annual miscellaneous fee for law students S$240 plus 9% GST. Fees are reviewed annually; the LLB fee sheet does not say they are fixed per cohort. 2025 fee sheet (updated 14 Feb 2025): SC S$46,640, PR S$74,600, without grant S$199,065.60, miscellaneous fee S$200. Official SUSS pages and PDFs read via a reader proxy (r.jina.ai/<official URL>) on 2026-10-01 because suss.edu.sg blocks automated access; sourceUrl is the official URL. Re-verified on 2026-10-01 (the law tuition-fees page now links only the Year 2025 and 2026 sheets). 2024 fee history: SUSS's 'Bachelor of Laws Year 2024 Programme Fees' sheet (updated 17 Feb 2023; linked as 'Year 2024 Bachelor of Laws' from the law tuition-fees page until early 2025, official URL suss.edu.sg/docs/default-source/contentdoc/sa/llb_programmefee.pdf, now removed), read from the Wayback Machine copy (snapshot 2024-07-02 14:09:15 UTC, web.archive.org/web/20240702140915/): with Tuition Grant, excl. GST, SC S$1,296 / PR S$2,590 per 5-cu course, Estimated Total Programme Fee SC S$46,640 and PR S$93,240; without Tuition Grant S$199,065.60 incl. GST; annual miscellaneous fee S$165 plus GST. Annual figures = total / 4.5.

programmes.notes: Whole-programme fee from SUSS's 'Year 2026/2027 Non-Subsidised Programme Fees (Graduate Programmes)' (updated Sept 2026): Master's Programme S$31,680 for Singapore Citizens/PRs and S$38,016 for other residents, both excluding GST; 9% GST added here (S$34,531.20 / S$41,437.44). Not MOE-subsidised (SSG subsidies for SC/PR not applied). 60 cu; international students take the accelerated track completed in 1 year, so the whole fee is taken as one year (SC/PR regular track is 1.5-4 years). Compulsory fees = annual miscellaneous fee S$20 (SC/PR/other residents) or S$530 (international Student's Pass holders) plus 9% GST. The Dec 2023 page captures link grad-prog-tuition-fee-year-2024.pdf?sfvrsn=853cbbb0_8, also not captured. Wayback also holds only a 301 (2024-07-18) for that Grad_Prog_..._2024_ file. Tuition-fees page captures (2023-12-11, 2024-02-27, 2024-05-27, 2024-09-19) only link the sheet with no intake wording. New source found but not usable: SUSS 'Year 2024 Course Fee - CET Graduate Modular Course' (suss.edu.sg/docs/default-source/contentdoc/ccpe/cet-grad-coursefee.pdf, 'Updated as at 01 January 2024', Wayback captures 20240329091215 and 20240712084655, read via the Google Docs viewer) prices graduate modular courses (not the master's programme) at S$2,398.00 (SC/PR) and S$2,877.60 (other residents) per 5-cu course without SSG funding, incl. 9% GST. Not estimated.

programmes.name: Master of Social Sciences
programmes.summary: Programme total including 9% GST, spread over 2 years. Not government-subsidised; Citizens and PRs pay a lower rate than other students. Plus annual miscellaneous fees.
programmes.notes: Whole-programme fee from SUSS's 'Year 2026/2027 Non-Subsidised Programme Fees (Graduate Programmes)' (updated Sept 2026): Social Sciences Master's Programme S$36,960 for Singapore Citizens/PRs and S$44,352 for other residents, excluding GST; with 9% GST S$40,286.40 / S$48,343.68, divided by 2 years. Not MOE-subsidised. SUSS states 60 cu plus a 10-cu applied research project within a 4-year maximum candidature; 2 years assumes the regular graduate load of 15-20 cu per semester. Compulsory fees = annual miscellaneous fee S$20 (SC/PR) or S$530 (international) plus 9% GST. programmes.name: Master of Psychology
programmes.summary: Yearly fee over 2 years, fixed for your intake. Citizens and PRs pay the Ministry of Education (MOE) subsidised rate; international students pay the full unsubsidised fee including 9% GST. Mostly part-time.
programmes.notes: MOE-subsidised taught master's (the Master of Social Sciences record is self-funded; this is the School of Humanities and Behavioural Sciences' government-subsidised alternative in the same field). Figures from SUSS's 'Government-Subsidised Graduate Programmes: Tuition Fees Per Annum' PDF (published 16 Jun 2026, linked as 'View Subsidy Information' for graduate-by-coursework programmes on the graduate tuition-fee page). Section (A) 'For New Students admitted in AY2026/AY2027', Psychology row: Singapore Citizen S$6,950 and Singapore PR S$14,100 per annum with MOE subsidy, excluding GST (GST is subsidised by MOE); subsidised international rate 'NA', so the 'international' tier is the published fee for students NOT in receipt of government subsidy for the Organisational Psychology track, S$61,638 for the whole programme excluding GST (the only track open to international applicants; the Forensic track is restricted to SC/PR and costs S$62,400 without subsidy). 9% GST added here for the international tier (S$67,185.42) and divided by 2 years; SC/PR non-subsidised whole-programme fee for reference: S$52,000 (Forensic) / S$51,140 (Organisational) excl. GST. Duration: 60 cu; minimum candidature 2 years, maximum 4 (SUSS programme page); the AY2024 sheet says the per-annum fee equals S$230/cu for SC and S$460/cu for PR, i.e. 30 cu a year, so 2 years = whole programme. Mostly part-time/blended evening and weekday-practicum programme (SUSS lists graduate fees as 'Full time/Part time'). MOE subsidy applies from the January 2025 semester (SUSS FAQ in the same PDF). Cohort-locked: SUSS says each new cohort pays the same fees per year throughout its candidature (FAQ 7: 'Tuition fees are determined on cohort basis'). Compulsory fees = annual miscellaneous fee S$20 (SC/PR) or S$530 (international Student's Pass holders) plus 9% GST. Fee history from sections (B) AY2025/AY2026 (SC S$6,950, PR S$13,900; non-subsidised S$50,280 SC/PR, S$60,336 international, whole programme excl. GST) and (C) AY2024/AY2025 (SC S$6,900, PR S$13,800; non-subsidised S$50,280 / S$60,336) of the same PDF; international history = S$60,336 x 1.09 / 2; the international miscellaneous fee was S$380 plus GST in 2024 and 2025 (SUSS graduate tuition-fee page, Wayback copy of 2025-02-17, and the Year 2025 graduate fee sheet) against S$530 from 2026. Official PDF read via a reader proxy (r.jina.ai/<official URL>) on 2026-10-01 because suss.edu.sg blocks automated access; sourceUrl is the official URL.

programmes.name: Juris Doctor (JD)
programmes.summary: Part-time evening law degree for graduates with work experience, Citizens and PRs only; not open to international students. Programme total spread over about 4 years at the subsidised rate, fixed for your intake.
programmes.notes: NOT OPEN TO INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: SUSS's law-programmes eligibility page states 'The Law programme is open to Singaporeans and Permanent Residents only. This programme is unable to enrol international students or non-citizens.' The 'international' tier is kept only because the schema requires it: it is the 'Estimated Total Programme Fee (Without MOE subsidy, including GST)' that SUSS publishes for any student without the MOE subsidy (e.g. a Citizen or PR who previously received government subsidy for a postgraduate programme, which SUSS says makes them ineligible), not an international-student fee. Part-time, evening programme: SUSS's School of Law brochure (Jan 2026) says both law degrees 'comprise classes conducted in the evenings', are modular and allow students 'to continue working'; SUSS offers no full-time law programme (checked 2026-10-01). Graduate-entry criteria (SUSS eligibility page and Jan 2026 brochure): Singapore Citizen or PR; at least a bachelor's degree AND 'substantial work experience'; the LNAT; a full CV of work experience from every applicant; Mother Tongue Language requirement; admission interview. SUSS gives preference to applicants with work experience in related fields (social work, law enforcement, prison service) or community-work involvement; MinLaw's 2016 press release set the school up for 'mature students with life and work experience seeking a mid-career switch to law' (at least 80% of the intake). SUSS states no minimum age (its JD subsidy FAQ says none is required for the subsidy either), but the degree-plus-work-experience requirement means this is not a school-leaver programme. Fees: SUSS School of Law 'Juris Doctor Year 2026 Programme Fees' (PDF updated 9 Jun 2026, linked as 'Year 2026 Juris Doctor' from the law tuition-fees page). From the July 2026 intake JD students get MOE-subsidised fees instead of the Tuition Grant. Fees are charged per course (MOE-subsidised, excl. GST: SC below 40 S$1,561 / PR S$2,487 per 5-cu course; SC aged 40+ pay S$625). SUSS's 'Estimated Total Programme Fee' (150 cu): SC below 40 S$46,840, PR S$74,600 (excl. GST, separately subsidised by the government); without MOE subsidy S$165,888 incl. 9% GST. Annual figure = published total programme fee / 4 years, SUSS's stated typical completion time (JD page: 'about 4 years' as JD students take no electives; all School of Law students must finish within a maximum of 6 years), so a slower student pays the same total over more years. July intake. Compulsory fees = annual miscellaneous fee for law students S$240 plus 9% GST. The 2026 fee sheet says course fees are cohort based, i.e. fixed at the year's fees when enrolled. 2025 fee sheet (updated 14 Feb 2025, Tuition Grant basis): SC S$38,880, PR S$62,160, without grant S$165,888, miscellaneous fee S$200. Official SUSS pages and PDFs read via a reader proxy (r.jina.ai/<official URL>) on 2026-10-01 because suss.edu.sg blocks automated access; sourceUrl is the official URL. GST, SC S$1,296 / PR S$2,590 per 5-cu course, Estimated Total Programme Fee SC S$38,880 and PR S$77,700; without Tuition Grant S$165,888 incl. GST; annual miscellaneous fee S$165 plus GST. Annual figures = total / 4.
